quizzes.title: 20.1 Module 20 Introduction: Hitler's War, 1939 to 1941
quizzes.description:
MODULE INTRODUCTION
Module Introduction: Hitler's War, 1939 to 1941
Survey · 2 questions · not graded
▼ ─ ▼ ─ ▼
Before you start

Welcome to Hitler’s War, 1939 to 1941. Answer the questions below before you open the first lesson. Your answers help your teacher see where the class is starting. This survey is not graded.

This module's goals:
  • Describe how Germany conquered Poland, Norway, and France in 1939 and 1940.
  • Explain why Britain fought on, how the Battle of Britain was won, and what the United States did to help.
  • Explain why Hitler attacked the Soviet Union in 1941 and weigh whether Dunkirk was a victory or a defeat.

questions.text: Before you read: Was Dunkirk a victory or a defeat? Give your first answer in two or three sentences. You will answer it again at the end of the module, so it is fine if your answer changes.
I have read this module's goals and I know what I am working toward this week.

answers.text: Yes, I have read them
Not yet, I will read them before the first lesson

quizzes.title: 20.7 Reading Quiz: Hitler's War, 1939 to 1941
quizzes.description:
READING QUIZ
Reading Quiz: Hitler's War, 1939 to 1941
7 questions · 7 points
▼ ─ ▼ ─ ▼
Before you start

This quiz covers both lessons and both primary sources for this module. It has 7 questions. Most ask you to work something out from what you read, not to find a sentence in the text. You may look back at the lessons and sources while you work.

HOW TO WORK
Read the two lessons and the two primary sources first, and keep your notes in My Notebook. Then answer the questions below.

questions.text: The best French and British armies moved north into Belgium when the Germans attacked on May 10. Why did this help the German plan?

answers.text: It drew the German tanks into Belgian cities, where they were slowed down
It gave the Allies a strong river line that the Germans could not cross
The main German thrust went through the Ardennes behind them and raced to the Channel, so the armies that had moved north were cut off
It forced Hitler to change his plan to a slower and more cautious one

questions.text: The lesson says the Allies had about as many tanks as the Germans, and many of theirs were better built. What actually made the difference?

answers.text: The French spread their tanks among the infantry, while the Germans massed theirs, gave them radios, and backed them with aircraft
The German tanks were much larger and carried heavier guns
The Allied tanks were kept in France and never sent north
The Germans had three times as many tanks as the Allies

questions.text: Lord Halifax declined to become prime minister on May 10, 1940, and Churchill took the post. Why does the lesson tell you to notice how narrow the choice was?

answers.text: It shows that the King had no say in who became prime minister
It shows that Halifax was a coward who had no part in later events
It shows that Britain’s choice of leader was settled long before May 1940
A different answer from one man on one afternoon would have given Britain a different leader, which shows how much can turn on a single decision

questions.text: Why do historians still argue about the German tanks’ halt before Dunkirk on May 24?

answers.text: No one knows whether the halt happened at all
Hitler approved the halt, but the evidence points to more than one possible reason, such as tired tanks, Goering’s boast, or saving armor for the rest of France
Hitler’s own memoirs explain it, but historians do not trust them
The British government later paid Hitler to order the halt

questions.text: Crowds welcomed the soldiers home from Dunkirk as winners. Why did Churchill say that “wars are not won by evacuations”?

answers.text: He thought the soldiers had not fought well enough at Dunkirk
He wished to ask the French to make peace with Germany
He believed the evacuation had been a mistake that should be hidden
He wanted to warn the country that the army was saved but its guns and tanks were not, and that the war was still to be won

questions.text: In September 1940 Hitler turned his bombers from the RAF airfields to London. Why was this a mistake?

answers.text: The airfields had been near their limit, and the pause let Fighter Command recover and fight on
London had no defenses, so the raids cost Germany nothing
The raids on London made Britain’s government ask for terms
The RAF had already been destroyed, so the change made no difference

questions.text: Directive No. 21 orders the army to crush Russia “even before the conclusion of the war against England.” What does that phrase show about Hitler’s thinking, and what did it risk?

answers.text: He believed Britain had already agreed to make peace
He wanted Britain and Russia to fight each other
He believed he could beat Russia quickly while Britain was still unbeaten, but he risked the long two-front war that German leaders had feared since 1914
He planned to wait many years before attacking Russia

discussions.title: 20.8 Discussion: Was Dunkirk a victory or a defeat?
discussions.html:
DISCUSSION
Was Dunkirk a victory or a defeat?
A rescue by sea, or the loss of an army’s equipment and a campaign?
Graded discussion · 10 points · one post and one reply
▼ ─ ▼ ─ ▼
HOW TO WORK
Read the two lessons and the two primary sources first, and look over your notes in My Notebook. Then post your answer to the prompt below, and reply to one classmate.
DISCUSSION PROMPT

This week’s question: Was Dunkirk a victory or a defeat?

Choose a side. Use the two-column list from your notebook. Give one fact from the lessons that supports calling Dunkirk a victory and one that supports calling it a defeat, then say which is stronger. Say what the British saved and what they left behind.

Write 150 to 250 words. State one claim you believe is true. Then explain why, using the specific evidence named above. Keep to what the lessons and the sources show. If you are guessing, say so.

Then add one sentence on courage. Britain stood alone in 1940. Does holding firm when yielding looks wiser always show courage, or can it be stubbornness? Say what you think and why.

RESPOND TO A CLASSMATE

Reply to one classmate. Do you agree with their reasoning? If so, strengthen it with a fact or decision they did not use. If not, say politely where you think it falls short, and give your reason.

GRADING RUBRIC (10 pts)
CriteriaSubstantive (full credit)Thin (partial credit)Missing (no credit)
Your claim and your reasons
6 pts		Takes a clear side, uses the specific evidence the prompt asks for, and explains why it supports the claim.Takes a side but gives general reasons, or leaves out part of what the prompt asks for.No post, or no claim.
